solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expire, though previously fit as a fiddle

parts.note: ex- means former or previous, as in ex-wife
hale means in robust health

explanation.surface: Someone dies despite having been in perfect health until then.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire is literally to breathe out, the original sense of the word.

clue.text: Suffers, made to conclude sure change is needed

parts.note: to end is to conclude

indicators.note: the word sure is rearranged, giving URES

explanation.surface: Someone endures being forced to finish a certain change.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer something is to bear or put up with it, a synonym.

clue.text: Game for a drink after hard work

indicators.note: the drink is placed after the two short pieces

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
op is short for opus, a musical work
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: Someone plays for a whisky reward after a day of heavy labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping across chalked squares.

clue.text: Behave uninhibitedly on the French tour

parts.note: le is the masculine French for the
a trip is a tour or journey

explanation.surface: Someone lets loose while on a holiday in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act without restraint, abandoning inhibition.

clue.text: Academic has rooms outside the university

indicators.note: the rooms sit outside, wrapping round the letter for the university

parts.note: studios are rooms, such as artists' workrooms or one-room flats
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A scholar has lodgings just beyond the university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic person is bookish and given to study, a near synonym.

clue.text: Captured and shot

definitions.meaning: photographed, as when a picture is snapped

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense means both seized and photographed, as in took a picture.

clue.text: Bed in new seed and provide an account

indicators.note: the word for bed goes inside the rearranged letters
the word seed is made new by rearrangement, giving DESE

parts.note: a crib is a child's bed or cot

explanation.surface: A gardening instruction about planting in a bed, then writing a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' looks like a flowerbed for the seed but is a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe is to give an account or report of something.

clue.text: Where to find a washer always available

definitions.meaning: a washer is a ring inside a tap
ready for use whenever needed, like beer on draught

explanation.definitionFit: A tap's washer sits literally in this place, and the idiom means ready whenever wanted.

clue.text: Tacks up a favourite piece from the paper

indicators.note: in a down clue this reads upwards, reversing the word

parts.note: tacks are drawing pins
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Pinning up a favourite newspaper cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small extract or cutting, such as one from a newspaper.

clue.text: Substitute a mine safety official

definitions.meaning: a stand-in who acts for someone else
in British coal mines this was the title of the official responsible for safety in a district of the pit

explanation.definitionFit: Both a stand-in and a pit safety officer go by this title.

clue.text: The poet Dante?

parts.note: the Victorian poet and painter Dante Gabriel ... shared the first name of the setter and of the Italian poet

explanation.walkthrough: The solver expects Alighieri, but the question mark points to another poet called Dante: the Pre-Raphaelite Dante Gabriel Rossetti.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was an English poet and Pre-Raphaelite painter.

clue.text: Fear led to new form of government

indicators.note: the letters are brought to a different form, rearranged

explanation.surface: Fear brought about a new kind of political system.
explanation.definitionFit: Federal is an adjective relating to central government in a union of states.

clue.text: Criminal who runs a bankrupt business

definitions.meaning: a fence, one who handles stolen goods
an official appointed to manage the affairs of an insolvent company

explanation.definitionFit: The same title names both a fence for stolen goods and an insolvency official.

clue.text: Be quiet and finish

definitions.meaning: an informal command to shut up
to conclude or round off a matter

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to shut up and to bring something to a close.

clue.text: Called for as arranged

explanation.definitionFit: The participle means both requested and put in sequence.

clue.text: Son of Adam said to sound archaic

indicators.note: the clue word is to be heard in its old biblical form, then that form spoken aloud

parts.note: the archaic biblical form of the verb of speaking is saith, as in 'thus saith the Lord'

explanation.surface: A question about a biblical figure whose name seems antique when spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly saith is the old form of 'says', not 'said', so the clue is loose; the blogger also found it uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis.

clue.text: Unstable German joined the Italian in bar

parts.note: Jerry is old British slang for a German

indicators.note: the Italian article goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: but means except, as does bar
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: A German man joins an Italian at a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning except, giving BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddily constructed buildings are rickety and liable to collapse, hence unstable.

clue.text: In which one lacks the will to benefit others

definitions.text: In which one lacks the will to benefit others

parts.words: In which one lacks the will to benefit others
parts.note: reads as selfishness, but the will is a legal testament leaving property to others

explanation.walkthrough: 'will' suggests willpower or goodwill; it is a testament, so this is dying without one.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal state of dying without a valid testament to pass on one's estate.

clue.text: In emergency, get a bugging device and move slowly

parts.note: a tap is a wiretap on a phone
to inch is to creep forward

explanation.surface: In a crisis, plant a listening device and edge forward carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means when necessary or in a crisis.

clue.text: Where eggs may be cooked for it

definitions.meaning: eggs are boiled or poached in heated water
British slang for being in trouble, as in 'you're for it now'

explanation.walkthrough: 'For it' is British slang meaning about to be punished.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in trouble also literally describes eggs boiling in a pan.

clue.text: Provides cover when the nurse is busy

indicators.note: the letters are made active and jumbled

explanation.surface: A hospital-shift picture: arranging cover while the nurse is occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer gives financial cover against loss.

clue.text: Bet backing a mount hotly tipped when it runs

definitions.text: a mount hotly tipped when it runs

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for a stake is read in reverse

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker before the deal

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse tipped as a hot favourite in its race.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing picture misleads: the 'mount' is a mountain, 'hotly tipped' its fiery summit, and it 'runs' when lava flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the Sicilian volcano, a mountain whose peak is hot and which erupts with flowing lava.

clue.text: A new role in flight control

indicators.note: the following letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a fresh job in air traffic control.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged surface on an aircraft's wing used to control roll.

clue.text: If here, has to be moved a little lower

indicators.note: the letters have to be shifted round into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift something a bit further down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' means not further down but a creature that lows, i.e. moos.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow is a small animal that moos.

clue.text: Jam — thinly applied?

definitions.meaning: a meagre layer of butter or margarine on bread

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tight spot and a thin smear of spread on toast.

clue.text: After a drink sailor gets up for a dance

indicators.note: the reversed sailor comes after the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, the traditional naval drink

indicators.note: in a down clue the word rises, so it is read backwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor has a drink and gets up to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Crossword addicts should be used to such a setback

definitions.text: Crossword addicts should be used to such a setback

parts.words: Crossword addicts should be used to such a setback
parts.note: solvers meet the device of words read backwards all the time, and the word also means a setback

explanation.walkthrough: Solvers often meet the device of reading letters backwards, and the same word means a reverse in fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn for the worse in one's fortunes is a setback.

clue.text: Support one throughout

annotationWithheld.why: Support one throughout (4): PIER is I inside PER, so 'throughout' gives PER ('through') and is also the container signal ('out'), one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Sentimental jerk in the Eternal City?

parts.note: Rome is called the Eternal City, so something belonging there is Roman
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A soppy fool is found living in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult for a person but is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes someone given to idealised, sentimental feelings.

clue.text: A very strong atmosphere of romance

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
air is atmosphere, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A love story with an intense, heady mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romance, typically a passing or illicit one.

clue.text: Beach shoes are adjusted for it

indicators.note: the letters are altered and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Beach footwear is modified to suit sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach is the strip of land beside the sea, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Little girl pinching little boy's pencil

indicators.note: squeezing between the fingers, so one name holds the other inside it

parts.note: Con is a short form of the girl's name Constance or Connie
Ray is a short form of the boy's name Raymond

explanation.surface: A small girl steals a small boy's pencil in the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' reads as stealing but means gripping round.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a coloured drawing pencil of wax or chalk.
